metadata.fatality_note: Total includes both AI users who died (16) and third-party victims killed by AI users (13: Margaux Whittemore, Suzanne Adams, 8 in Tumbler Ridge mass shooting including stepbrother Emmett Jacobs age 11, Robert Morales 57 and Tiru Chabba 45 in FSU mass shooting, and Angela Shellis 45 killed by her son using DeepSeek for weapon selection in Wales)
metadata.taxonomy_note: Cases classified by mechanism_type (relational_pathway, cognitive_pathway, instrumental_pathway) and outcome_target (self_harm, violence_against_others)

mechanism_definitions.relational_pathway: Emotional dependency, parasocial attachment, or companion relationship contributed to psychological deterioration and lethal outcome
mechanism_definitions.cognitive_pathway: AI validated, reinforced, or amplified delusional, psychotic, or disordered thinking leading to lethal action
mechanism_definitions.instrumental_pathway: AI provided operational assistance, tactical information, or capability that enabled lethal violence as a tool/resource

metadata.verification_standard: Court documents, multiple independent news sources, or official government acknowledgment

perpetrator.name: Tristan Roberts
perpetrator.status: Convicted; sentenced to life imprisonment, minimum 22 years 6 months, Mold Crown Court, March 25, 2026

key_factors: First documented homicide case involving DeepSeek (Chinese general-purpose AI; 8th platform tracked in this database)
Roberts queried DeepSeek for advice suited to 'a non-experienced killer', specifically asking whether a knife or hammer would be more effective
DeepSeek initially declined to answer; Roberts circumvented the refusal by claiming he was writing a book about serial killers
DeepSeek then provided a comparative analysis of knife vs. hammer and recommended a hammer for an inexperienced killer
Roberts planned the murder for at least three weeks; documented intent extensively across 16 Discord accounts, retaining thousands of screenshots
On October 23, 2025 (10 days after his 18th birthday), Roberts lured his mother from their home under the pretext of seeking medical help, then walked her to the Morfa nature reserve
Attack lasted approximately 11pm to 3:30am; a dictaphone recording captured more than two hours during which Angela Shellis pleaded for her life
Court characterized motivation as misogyny and 'hatred of women'; Judge Rhys Rowlands at sentencing: 'You appear to have revelled in the control you exerted over your own mother'
Same instrumental-pathway taxonomy as the FSU shooting (April 2025) and Tumbler Ridge mass shooting (February 2026)
incidents.legal_action: Criminal conviction: guilty plea to murder; sentenced to life imprisonment with a minimum term of 22 years 6 months at Mold Crown Court (Wales), Judge Rhys Rowlands presiding, March 25, 2026
sources: Crown Prosecution Service Cymru Wales statement (March 2026)
Mold Crown Court conviction (guilty plea, March 25, 2026)

incidents.name: Jesse van Rootselaar
incidents.interaction_duration: Months (flagged June 2025, banned, created new account)

victims.includes: Mother (age 39), stepbrother Emmett Jacobs (age 11), education assistant (age 39), 5 students aged 12-13

key_factors: Largest-casualty instrumental-pathway case documented (8 killed, 2 wounded)
Second documented instrumental-pathway incident chronologically (FSU shooting April 2025 predates it by ~10 months)
OpenAI detected and banned account in June 2025 (8 months before shooting) via automated tools and human review of activity 'in furtherance of violent activities'
OpenAI stated the activity did not meet its threshold for notifying law enforcement 'because it didn't identify credible or imminent planning'
NO alert sent to RCMP at time of ban
WSJ reported internal debate among ~12 staff; some were alarmed enough to consider alerting law enforcement; company decided not to refer
Van Rootselaar created a second account that evaded detection until police released the shooter's name post-incident
OpenAI contacted RCMP only AFTER the February 2026 mass shooting

Canadian AI Minister Evan Solomon summoned OpenAI representatives to Ottawa to explain the June 2025 ban and the decision not to refer; minister publicly stated he was 'disappointed' that OpenAI 'did not have substantial answers'
Incident triggered national debate in Canada re: mandatory LE reporting for AI companies when threats are detected
Some researchers criticized OpenAI's subsequent 'safety pledges' as surveillance infrastructure rather than AI regulation
incidents.legal_action: Criminal investigation by RCMP; civil suit filed in 2026 by family of a critically wounded victim (referenced in NPR April 21, 2026); Canadian federal government exploring mandatory LE-referral policy for AI companies
incidents.verification_level: Official government acknowledgment and company admission

additional_context.openai_response_pre_shooting: Account detected and banned June 2025 via automated tools + human review; threshold for alerting law enforcement was NOT met by OpenAI's internal assessment because activity was not deemed 'credible or imminent' planning — no alert sent to RCMP
additional_context.openai_response_post_shooting: Contacted RCMP with information about van Rootselaar's account only after the February 2026 mass casualty event; stated this was 'proactive' sharing
additional_context.canadian_government_response: AI Minister Evan Solomon summoned OpenAI to Ottawa; following the meeting, Solomon stated publicly: 'We were disappointed that they did not have substantial answers for us, and we asked them to have substantial answers.'
additional_context.policy_debate: Active national debate in Canada re: whether AI companies should be required to report credible threats to law enforcement; OpenAI's post-incident 'safety pledges' announced in response criticized by some researchers as surveillance infrastructure rather than AI regulation
additional_context.second_account: Undetected until police released shooter's name post-shooting
additional_context.significance: First case where AI company explicitly acknowledged prior detection of violent planning; largest-casualty instrumental-pathway incident in the database; prompted first national-government-level intervention (Canadian minister summoning AI company for an accounting)

legislation.name: GUARD Act
legislation.full_name: Guidelines for User Age-verification and Responsible Dialogue Act of 2025
key_provisions: Prohibits minors from accessing AI companion chatbots
Requires disclosure that chatbot is AI at start of each conversation and at 30-minute intervals
Criminal penalties (up to $100,000) for bots that solicit or encourage minors to engage in sexual conduct, suicide, or violence
